additionalProperties.value: OSOS_ABORT_ENTRY: reviewed native patch site for the build-selected OSOS shim.
Returns when the platform predicate is false; otherwise invokes software interrupt 0x123456 and waits indefinitely.

Programs AES MMIO at 38c00000. Returns 0x28 for zero bytes, 9 for nonmultiple-of-16 length or unsupported key selector. Selector 0 loads a supplied 16-byte key; selectors 1/2 use hardware selection. Loads supplied 16-byte IV in register byte order, or zero IV when null, programs input/output and starts hardware. Direction is reduced to zero/nonzero. Returns 0 after submission; this body contains no completion poll.

Lazily allocates/initializes an 8-byte mutex, locks it, calls Crypto_AESProcessBufferHardware with all seven arguments, unlocks and returns hardware status. Can allocate and block; unsuitable for an allocation-free PCM callback without a broader execution-context design.
Returns 1 if the song already owns a private extension or allocates one from its owner's 0x30-byte extension pool and stores it at record +0x10. Returns 0 on invalid owner or allocation failure.

Returns the logical 64-bit position of a buffered file, accounting for unread buffer contents in forward or reverse mode. Clears position before querying. Returns zero on success or the underlying file status.

Matches UTF-16 artist prefixes against database entries at +0xba4/+0xba8. Writes count-prefixed UTF-16 to output when nonnull, rewriting a matching prefix or copying the original text. Clamps character_count to 255. Returns 1 for a matched prefix, otherwise 0.
Unregisters the child using its slot byte at +1, zeros its 0xf00-byte storage and frees it. Caller releases cached arrays and vectors before destruction.

Compares two counted UTF-16 strings using the supplied collation context and native comparison options. Lazily initializes the global option word to 0x1d. Returns the underlying comparator's negative, zero or positive result.

Skips leading control/space units, puts empty strings after nonempty strings and compares remaining UTF-16 using the supplied native option bits. The collation argument is unused by this implementation.

Compares the selected metadata field of two song records, returning negative, zero or positive. Artist mask 4 reads ordinary Artist from owner cache +0x118 and record token +0x2c; string fields use native collation. The 64-bit field mask is stack-passed after the unused r3 alignment slot.
Copies one entry at the requested index among browser-filtered songs, using the supplied native order and reversal.

Copies a media-list entry into the destination list. The third argument is an insertion cursor, validated by MediaList_ValidateInsertionCursor and passed to MediaList_LinkEntryAfterCursor. Normal OTG append callers pass NULL. Handles nested entries, duplicate suppression, allocation, and notifications.

Enumerates source in the requested order and copies accepted entries into destination, applying browser filters and playback skip rules. Optionally returns the copied entry at the selected filtered index. Shared by playback and On-The-Go.
Validates TrackData, notifies listeners, unlinks it from its database, destroys media lists and storage, then clears and frees the allocation.
Null returns -50. Otherwise destroys the embedded path value at +4, frees the surrounding 16-byte object, and returns 0. Used in context cleanup and failed storage initialization.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Calls registry initializer 082d13d0 once, guarded by a global byte, then returns 0. Called before looking up/claiming storage context records. No locking is visible in this wrapper.

Opens the path descriptor for writing, stages bytes in temporary storage, writes the requested length and updates file length after a full write. Releases temporary/file resources on exit. Returns zero on success, -50 for invalid arguments, -43 on open failure, or a write failure code; a null buffer is allowed only for zero bytes.
Looks up a numeric artwork ID in the database's lazily built sorted index, with a linked-list fallback. Returns the artwork entry or null.
Returns the record's numeric artwork ID from its artwork entry at +0xc, or zero. The owner holds the artwork database at +0xf9c.
Returns the explicit list at +4, or the owner's default list at +0xf44/+0xf48 when unset.
Returns browser itself for kind 1, its +0xefc owner for kind 2, otherwise null.
Returns the numeric artwork ID at +0xc of a 24-byte album row in this browser's +0xeb0 vector, or zero for an invalid index.
Returns the entry at a zero-based ordered index, or NULL for an invalid list/index or unavailable cache. Normalizes order/reversal and lazily builds the order cache.
Reads the album group's first token from TrackData's Album cache +0x1c8 into counted UTF-16 (up to 255 units). Output must be nonnull. Returns native cache status or -50.
Reads the artist group's first token from TrackData's Artist/Composer cache +0x118. Writes up to 255 UTF-16 units after the output count. Output must be nonnull. Returns native cache status or -50.

For a valid Artist row, returns the owner's Artist jump-table letter as counted UTF-16. Uses owner +0xe50, falling back to the full Artist name when no jump table exists. Output needs 256 UTF-16 units; returns 0 or -50.
Builds album groups using field mask 2, or 0x80000000 for compilations. Returns zero on failure, otherwise the number of 24-byte rows at +0xeb0..+0xeb4.
Builds grouped values for Artist field mask 4 using the native artist-group callback. Returns zero on a build error, otherwise the number of 20-byte entries in the vector at +0xe64..+0xe68.
Reads the browser's two-bit match state from entry +0x1c using the browser slot byte at +1: 0 unevaluated, 1 accepted, 2 rejected.

Maps a linked entry to its zero-based ordered index, normalizing order/reversal. Lazily builds the forward index and inverse map at list+0x470+4*mode. Returns -1 for invalid input or an unavailable map.

Prepares the random hardware, seeds it once at MMIO 0x3c100008 using RTC bytes, a platform value, timer register and incoming r4, then discards 19 warm-up words. Reads one result and restores the prior gate state. Later calls skip seeding. Incoming r4 contributes to the seed in the actual instructions; entropy quality is not established.

Reads display-artist token +0x30 from owner cache +0x170 when enabled by database +8 -> +0xb0f; otherwise reads ordinary Artist. Writes count-prefixed UTF-16 into a 512-byte output buffer and returns the cache-read status.
Maps browser sort selector +0xe38 to native order mode. Artist selector 1 maps to mode 7; Album selector 3 maps to mode 6.
Returns the current global entry-ID counter, then increments it for the next allocation.
Returns bit 0 of the imported SysInfo flags at offset 0x94.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Returns the heap base from literal 0804b44c (stock 08b32b58) and size = SysInfo RAM base + RAM size - heap base. Caller 0806be98 passes the region to the main memory-pool initializer.
Initial heap region starts at native DRAM BSS end 0x08b3b1b0. CFW moves this bound to 0x08c2c000.
For zero delay_value, dispatches to the scheduler yield veneer. Otherwise forwards (0, delay_value) to the delay veneer. Delay units are not established by this wrapper.
Forwards context to FairPlay_ReleaseDecryptionContext and returns its status. The two status multipliers multiply to 1 modulo 2^32. This adapter is used at the game/media integration boundary.
Allocates and initializes a 0xf00-byte child browser and stores its owner at +0xefc. Returns 0 or -108 on allocation failure; browser registration has four slots.
Frees cached album token/jump arrays, clears album rows and selection, and resets compilation-only mode.
Frees artist token/jump arrays and each row's artwork array, clears the artist vector and resets index/text selection.
Frees cached song-entry and jump arrays and clears the song count.
Clears the current list's cached filtering flag and per-entry match states for this browser when cached results exist. Returns 0 or the traversal error.
Calls deleting destructor on nonzero/non-minus-one native file handle; returns zero.
Invokes the deleting destructor for handles other than NULL and -1. Returns zero.
r0={uint16 volume,char path[258]}, r1=data fourcc (unused here), r2=mode 1 read or 2/3 write, r3=handle output. Return r0 zero on success.

Opens the volume-prefixed path descriptor: uint16 volume followed by path bytes. Mode 1 reads; 2/3 write. Writes the allocated handle on success and returns zero; invalid arguments return -50. file_type is unused. Frees failed opens and maps native errors.
r0 native file handle, r1 buffer, r2 bytes, r3 flags, stack argument uint32 bytes-read output. Zero success; flags 0 uses normal read.

Reads from a legacy handle into buffer and reports the byte count. Flags bit 1 selects the alternate read path. Returns zero on success; maps native file errors to legacy status values. Rejects handle -1 or NULL buffer with -50.
r0 native file handle, r1 buffer, r2 bytes, r3 flags, stack argument uint32 bytes-written output. Zero success; flag 1 calls native flush.

Writes buffer to a legacy handle and reports the byte count. Flags bit 0 flushes after a successful write. Returns zero on success and maps native file errors; rejects handle -1 or NULL buffer with -50.
Validates TrackData and acquires read access to its 24 string caches. Pair with TrackData_ReleaseStringCaches.
Releases a default-heap allocation and updates heap accounting under the heap guard. Null is a no-op; an invalid allocation header aborts.
Allocates zero-filled storage from the default heap with allocation tag 4. Returns the allocation pointer or null.
Allocates count*8+12 bytes for a jump index and writes count into its first word. Rows hold a UTF-16 label and list index; the extra pair permits a sentinel. Returns null on allocation failure.

Allocates a song from the fixed-size record pool at TrackData +0x44. Sets its owner, kind, generated ID, shared default extension and supplied timestamp (or generates one when zero), then links it into TrackData. Returns NULL on allocation failure or count limit; reserved is unused.

Allocates a 16-byte descriptor and a 0x2000-byte aligned workspace split into two 0x1000-byte pages. Stores wrapper, page pointers and page size, then publishes descriptor. Returns -108 if descriptor allocation fails, otherwise zero. Nested aligned allocation is assumed successful.
Loads preferences at state+4, marks readiness at +0xbef, and migrates older records to schema 0x3f. Resets invalid records and initializes newly introduced fields.

Allocates an import reader, opens and validates the library file, and imports its track and playlist datasets. The reader stores its file at +0x40000 and TrackData owner at +0x40004. Returns zero on success or a native error status.
Invalidates and rebuilds order mode 2, then assigns consecutive song ranks 1..count in its existing order. Assumes rebuilding succeeds; does not choose a new random order.

Reads one full block from storage interface 0, then copies the requested in-block slice to output. Validates offset and slice bounds, resolves record to a block address, wipes/releases the temporary block and balances resource 0x33. Returns zero on success or -1. Used for sidr digest storage; underlying medium is not established here.

Reads one full block from storage interface 0, compares the requested slice, and rewrites the block only when bytes differ. Validates bounds, wipes/releases temporary storage and balances resource 0x33. Returns zero on success or -1. This is a persistent storage mutation, not a RAM-only digest update.

Lazily allocates a mutex and serializes SHA-1 backend access. Flag bit 0 at +0x50 selects fresh initialization versus state restore; feeds input then bit 1 selects final digest versus intermediate-state save to +0x4c. Unlocks and returns zero. Helper results are not propagated.

Stores the selected album index at +0x18 and its counted UTF-16 name at +0x62c; -1 clears it. Invalidates dependent groups, songs and entry matches while preserving the artist filter. Returns 0 or -50.

Stores the selected artist index at +0x10 and its counted UTF-16 name at +0x22c; -1 clears it. Invalidates albums, dependent groups, songs and cached entry matches. Returns 0 or -50 for an invalid index.
Selects a list from owner +0xf64/+0xf68, storing pointer/index at browser +4/+8. Clears metadata groups, selected values, songs and cached entry matches. Returns 0 or -50.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Converts the EQ menu index with EQ_MenuIndexToSettingsId, updates uint16 settings+0xb64 if changed, persists/notifies through 08053794, and calls the player EQ method at vtable+0xa0 with the low byte. Returns zero. The default decompiler signature includes scratch-register inputs; the true ABI needs caller confirmation.
Replaces the two-bit match state assigned to this browser in entry +0x1c.
Updates the browser-slot bit in list +0x1ad. Tracks whether per-entry match bits for this browser require invalidation.
Walks 21 task descriptors of 20 bytes twice: first creates every configured task, then starts them. The table includes GraphicsManager, so UI tasks may run before startup returns.

Requires nonnull base/name/output and encoded strlen divisible by four. Decodes each group as [in2^ca,in0^a6,in3^01,in1^4a], appends it to base in a newly allocated 16-byte path object, and classifies its storage mode at +0xc. On success writes output_path and returns 0; invalid inputs/allocation path return an error. Wipes/frees the temporary decoded name. Used for IC-Info.sidb/sidd/sidv/sidr/sidl and IC-Info.rbSyncResp.
Validates TrackData and releases read access to its 24 string caches acquired by TrackData_AcquireStringCaches.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Resolves the opaque storage handle through 083424b4. Record +0xc controls release: zero skips destruction, one destroys owned parsed objects +0x60..0x70, all six path objects +0xa0..0xb4 and allocated base path +8, clearing those pointers and identity state. Larger counts take the reference-decrement path. Returns a 32-bit status; the decompiler second return word is incidental register state.

Returns the decoded format word stored at context +8, or zero for a null context. The protected sample-entry parser uses this as the replacement sample format after successful context creation; the stored word is encoded, not a plain FourCC.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Obfuscated front end used by media and game loading. Rejects null context with 0xffff5bd9 and a context+0x10 encoded-flag condition with 0xffff5bc6. Builds request {context,input,output,reserved,bytes,0,0} for 0831bf88 and returns its status unchanged. Constant products on byte count and final status reduce to identity modulo 2^32. Input/output may alias as the game caller does.

Optionally reads wall-clock day/seconds fields and writes sign-extended 32-bit Unix seconds: (day-2440588)*86400 + seconds. A second optional output uses cached day/seconds as day*86400 + seconds. Returns zero or mapped clock-read error. Arithmetic is 32-bit before sign extension; the second output's epoch is not established here.

Creates/reuses a storage registry record for base_path and returns its opaque numeric handle through output_handle. Identity inputs are length-prefixed byte strings; library caller supplies 8 device bytes, game caller 6 bytes. Initializes six IC-Info path objects and refreshes storage with selector 0x10. Record +8 owns the base path, +0xc tracks references, +0x60..0x70 hold parsed objects, and +0xa0..0xb4 hold paths. Returns status and cleans partial path allocations on failure. Internal identity/flag validation remains obfuscated.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Validates all three pointers (-50 on null), checks embedded path existence (-43 if absent), loads file contents, allocates/copies a caller-owned buffer and returns pointer/size with status 0. Allocation failure returns -108. Marks path-object byte 0 on success and destroys temporary file wrappers. Caller releases output_data through 08023ef0.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Resolves storage_handle and calls 082de3c8 with .sinf bytes, mode, options and parsed registry objects to produce a per-stream decryption context. Media parser 0809d6c4 passes a complete sinf atom, options 0/0 and mode 1, then stores successful context in a mode-3 crypto slot. If record +0x6c has dirty byte +0x21, serializes/persists it through sidr path +0xac; persistence failure releases the newly created context. Frees serialized temporary data and returns status. Option semantics are unresolved; may allocate and write storage.
Reads byte_count bytes from the file object at reader +0x40000 into destination. Rejects lengths above 0x40000 with -0xd0. Returns the file-read status.

Advances the import stream at reader +0x40000. Positive counts are read and discarded in chunks up to 1024 bytes; negative counts seek relative to the current 64-bit position. Returns zero on success or the file status.

Fills a clipped rectangle with a solid RGBA color, converting to the surface pixel format. Mode 0x22 handles partial alpha. GraphicsContext_FillRect calls this at 0825ae9c; bitmap blitting is separate.
Sends the low byte of r0 using SYS_WRITEC (3), SVC 0x123456.
Writes the low byte of character using semihosting SYS_WRITEC (3), SVC 0x123456. Requires a semihosting handler.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Gets the platform heap region, stores its base/size at manager offsets +0xd8/+0xdc, then calls 080cc0bc to initialize the memory pool.
Returns arithmetic_shift_right_16(low32(sample*gain_q15)<<1). Used for speed overlap fades. Computes in 32 bits without saturation, so valid fixed-point ranges are a caller requirement.

Reads Manifest.plist with a null signature path, selects an executable by platform ID/version, requires a nonempty Name, and copies Version, UserDataPath, localized names, and optional LaunchingArtwork.
Allocates zero-filled storage from the default heap, forwarding allocation_tag to the heap allocator. Returns the allocation pointer or null.
Enables SHA engine resource, clears MMIO 0x38000004/10 and the 64-bit byte counter, then sets engine_control=2 for initial processing. Does not process input or acquire the global SHA mutex itself.

Appends SHA-1 0x80/zero padding and big-endian 64-bit bit length to the partial block, submits one or two blocks, copies 20 digest bytes from hardware and releases engine resource. Mutates partial block and control; caller holds the shared SHA mutex.

Builds and caches the ordered array of matching song entries at +0xeec, optional jump index at +0xef0 and count at +0xef4. Uses MediaBrowser_EvaluateEntryFilters for every candidate. Returns 0 or a negative status.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Returns logical Hold state: 1 locked, 0 unlocked. Converts raw 0/1 from 082da704 to 1 - raw; other values return 0.
Runtime heap lower bound, paired with 0x0804b478. CFW reserves [0x08b3c000, 0x08c2c000) for its payload.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Allocates a 24-byte message, stores tone parameters at +0x10/+0x14, and posts event 5 to task/queue 2 through 0802d058. Alarm and alert callers use pairs including (540,200) and (676,200).

Appends one selection, or the whole source list for index -1, to On-The-Go. Enforces the 1000-entry limit, mirrors additions into the active OTG playback list, and marks preferences dirty. Returns zero on success or -41 when unavailable/full.

Adds bytes to the 64-bit count, submits aligned full blocks to SHA DMA at MMIO 0x38000080/84/8c, splitting runs above 0xffc0 bytes. Polls engine busy bit after submissions, copies the remaining 0..63 bytes into partial_block, and switches control to continuation value 10. Blocking hardware path; synchronization is external.

Builds and caches distinct values from filtered, ordered song entries. Artist mask 4 uses order mode 7, ordinary Artist token +0x2c and the native text comparator; compilation handling follows the stock setting. Invokes an optional progress callback per accepted entry. Returns zero or a negative status. The 64-bit mask occupies r2/r3; the callback is on the stack.
Increments the cache-use counter at +0x30, allowing borrowed token access and preventing cache mutation while held. Returns zero or -0x32 for an invalid cache.
Allocates an entry from list+0x3c, sets its owner and a new global entry ID, and clears the first flags byte at +0x1c. Returns NULL on allocation failure.
Temporarily replaces the last byte with NUL, emits SYS_WRITE0, then emits and restores that byte. Requires writable input.
Emits a nonempty writable span through semihosting. Temporarily replaces the final byte with NUL for SYS_WRITE0, writes that saved byte with SYS_WRITEC, then restores it. length must be positive.

Formats and draws text into the caller's pixel buffer using a native 2D context: 320x240 bounds, 0x280-byte row stride, 16-bit depth. Called after the game frame callback with runtime+0x38 as the buffer.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Translates executable addresses 0x18000000..0x180fffff through descriptor 08a10718. Other addresses pass through unchanged.

Copies five SHA state MMIO words from 0x38000020 as 20 little-endian bytes to output, then disables/releases engine resource (1,0). The state argument is unused by this leaf. Caller arranges completion and synchronization.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Nonreturning media reader worker. Obtains packets from provider vtable +0x1c, processes protected bytes through crypto slot 1 into the shared output buffer, and uses IRAM fallback 220084dc when slot mode is zero. Releases each provider packet through +0x20, submits output to consumer +0x40, and posts timing/state metadata and end-of-stream messages. Waits on global synchronization between runs; this is upstream of PCM effects, not an in-place PCM callback.

Inserts a node using cursor {parent, predecessor}. NULL appends under the list root; predecessor -1 selects the tail, 0 inserts at the head, and other values insert after that node. Node fields: +4 parent, +8 next, +0xc previous. Updates root/ancestor counts and invalidates order caches.
Reads native BMap format, depth and stride; uses resource+28 as pixel/palette storage when payload length at +24 is nonzero, then initializes the surface.
Initializes data pointer, stride, pixel depth, format, bounds and surface locking state. Indexed format 0x64 uses 8-bit indices; format 0x1888 uses 32-bit pixels.

Imports mhlp/mhyp playlists and mhip members. Detects MHOD 52/53 in the metadata pass, then seeks back after creating members to import order arrays and jump tables. Uses ITunesDB_MapSortType for database sort selectors. Returns native status. Reader layout follows ITunesDB_ImportLibrary.

Imports mhlt/mhit tracks and understood MHOD values into TrackData. MHOD 22 dispatch at 0x0808adcc discards its payload through 0x0808b184. Reader file and owner remain at +0x40000/+0x40004; record persistent ID remains at +0x110/+0x114. Returns zero or an error status.
Album Artist MHOD 22 dispatch. Native branch skips the payload; CFW retains it using reader r7, record r4 and body length [sp+0x228] - [sp+0x224]. Returns to 0x0808b120 with status in r0.
Stores the MHOD handler status in r10 and continues the import loop.
Maps kinds 0/4 to games_RO, 1 to gamedata_RW, 2 to gamestats_WO, and 3 to gamedata_ShareRW. Unknown kinds return the empty suffix string.

Enables the SHA engine resource and loads five words from state_output into MMIO 0x38000020..30. Sets engine_control to 10 for continuation. Caller serializes hardware access and supplies the state words.

Positive byte_count reads and discards bytes in a 1024-byte temporary buffer; negative counts seek relative to the current 64-bit file position. Returns zero on success or the file status. Used by the iTunesDB importer for ignored text types including Album Artist (22); retains no metadata payload.

Initializes a caller-owned 0x58-byte cache and registers its pointer in the global cache list. Flag 1 enables reference-counted deduplication; flag 4 allocates hash tables, falling back when allocation fails. flags 0xf matches the native artist/composer caches. Returns zero or -0x32 for incompatible flags. The registered cache object must remain alive.
Validates the cache, frees token storage and hash allocations, and zeros its 0x58-byte object. Returns zero or -0x32 for an invalid cache. Outstanding borrowed views and tokens expire.
Returns a borrowed token payload and byte count through optional outputs. Caller must hold cache read access, including for token zero. Forwards zero or -0x32 from the token-view lookup.
Sorts index entries using the native fields for order_mode. Mode 2 compares song shuffle ranks at entry+0x24. Brackets sorting with database allocation-update guards.
Decrements a positive cache-use counter at +0x30. Returns zero, or -0x32 for an invalid cache or an unbalanced release.

Reads a 16-bit length prefix and text following it, creates a temporary string and matches the 22 stock English preset names. Returns stored ID 100..121; null, empty and unknown names return 0. Destroys the temporary string on all matching and fallthrough paths.

Builds game paths. Arguments: output native string object, directory kind, game-identifier native string, storage-mode flag, relative-path C string. For kind 0, flag 0 selects iPod_Control/games_RO/<identifier>/<relative>; nonzero selects Resources/Games/games_RO/<identifier>/<relative>. Other kinds select gamedata_RW, gamestats_WO, or shared storage. Native strings use the two-word ABI.
Initializes defaults, opens the native preferences path, reads at most 0xb90 bytes, and updates two cached globals. Closes the handle after reading; failed opens retain defaults.

Scans child atoms after the sample-entry header for sinf. Supports p608/drmi/drms/drmt headers of 0x20/0x66/0x34/0x3e bytes. Rebuilds the complete sinf atom in temporary storage and creates a media decryption context. Success stores slot mode 3/context and returns the decoded media format; failed creation retains the supplied format. Frees sinf storage and seeks to entry offset+0x18 after a found sinf. Unsupported formats return zero. Output on malformed/missing sinf follows the last atom type, so this is not a boolean success API.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Finds a game API module by its 32-byte name in the linked registry at 08a0fc88..08a1070c. Modules: Audio, Metadata, SoundEffect, AsyncFileIO, MemoryAlloc, InputEvents, Settings, OpenGLES, Users, DebugUtil, and miscTBD.
Returns arithmetic_shift_right_16(low32(sample_a*gain_a_q15 + sample_b*gain_b_q15)<<1). Speed overlap passes complementary weights. No saturation or wider accumulation is performed.
Maps raw wheel position to (((119 - (raw & 0xbfffffff)) * 8 / 3) & 0xff) | (raw & 0x40000000). Bit 30 is the contact flag used by InputWheel_AccumulateMotion.

Copies up to maximum_bytes from a live token into destination while holding the cache-use counter at +0x30. Writes the copied byte count through byte_count when nonnull. Token zero succeeds with zero bytes. Returns zero or -0x32; outputs are valid on success.
Normalizes list order mode. Playback traversal mode 0x33 resolves to list+0xc8 when list+0x18c bit 0 is clear, or mode 2 when set. Mode 0 falls back to 1.
Arguments: serial context, byte count, buffer. Uses context port at +1; writes UART TX register +0x20 in chunks up to 16 bytes under a semaphore.
OSOS_EQ_MAP_ENTRY: reviewed native patch site for the build-selected OSOS shim.
Maps stored IDs 100..121 to DSP presets 1..22; every other ID returns bypass preset 0. Flat (ID 107) maps to preset 8, so Flat and Off have distinct preset identities.

Copies up to 510 token bytes into output+1 and writes the UTF-16 code-unit count into output[0]. Caller supplies 512 bytes. Returns the cache-read status; output is valid on success. Token zero produces an empty string.

Reads a MHOD 52 payload into buffer. Converts its sort type to a native order mode, requires count to match list tracks, and resolves zero-based positions against list order 1. Installs the resulting RAM entry array at list +0x3ac+4*mode. Returns read status; unsupported types or invalid positions are skipped. No file write.

Releases a cache token reference; token zero is a no-op. With flag 1, the slot is marked reclaimable only when its reference count reaches zero. Refuses invalid tokens or a busy/read-only cache. Returns zero on success or -0x32.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Reverse lookup of the 23 uint32 EQ IDs at 083e2568. r0=stored ID, r1=uint32 output pointer. Writes menu index, or -1 and returns -50 on failure.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.
Searches all 23 EQ IDs at 083e2568. Writes matching menu index and returns 0. Unknown ID writes 0xffffffff and returns -50; null output also returns -50.

Builds 24-byte album rows from adjacent Album tokens, retaining representative Artist/DisplayArtist tokens, artwork and track count. For compilation albums with differing Artists, substitutes a shared artist token and clears DisplayArtist. Returns callback continuation status.

Appends 20-byte Artist groups in incoming order using native collation. Stores Artist/DisplayArtist tokens and up to ten artwork pointers; album-transition counting stops when that artwork cap is reached. Skips compilation tracks when the stock setting is enabled. Returns 1 to continue, 0 when an existing result stops callbacks.

Initializes TrackData string caches and fixed-size pools: 0x120-byte song records and 0x30-byte extensions. Artist and Composer share the reference-counted cache at +0x118 with flags 0xf. Returns zero or an allocation error.
Maps database sort types to native list order modes. Type 4 (album) ->6; type 5 (artist) ->7; 0x23 ->0x2d; 0x24 ->0x2f; 0x25 ->0x2e. Unsupported types return zero. Same mapping as 2.0.4 at 080cba70.

Returns a borrowed token payload through optional data and byte_count outputs, clearing both first. Requires positive cache-use count unless allow_unpinned is nonzero. Token zero succeeds with empty outputs. Returns zero or -0x32 for invalid cache/token or missing read access.

For a valid cache, frees hash buckets and tables when forced or flags 4 and 8 are both set. Clears flag 4 and sets read-only flag 0x40. Returns zero, or -0x32 for an invalid cache; retained string tokens remain readable.
Allocates capacity*4+0x14 bytes, records capacity and allocation size, and initializes count to zero. Returns NULL on allocation failure.

Programs SHA DMA mode=1 and length=64, writes engine control, polls the busy bit until clear, then writes the block address and sets continuation control=10. The visible poll precedes the address write; this leaf alone does not establish completion after that write. Does not update byte count.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Imports a string MHOD through 080b3458. output_encoding 1 uses the UTF-16 cache path and writes the resulting token; the on-disk decoder accepts UTF-16LE (1) and UTF-8 (2). glyph_field selects the native glyph bitmap populated by 081c2ae8; collect_characters updates the importer character set except for location type 2. Returns zero on success or an error status. The 2.0.4 CFW Album Artist hook invokes it for MHOD 22 with its own cache.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Imports up to 256 big-endian bytes after internal digest decoding byte*0xb5-0xdc. Encodes limbs/count and normalizes high zero limbs. Returns zero or length error; the input encoding differs from ordinary bytes accepted by BigIntImportPlain.

XORs each byte with 0xc6 in place for signed positive length. Used around the obfuscated transform wrappers. Applying the same operation twice restores the input; there is no local pointer or capacity validation.

Decodes the input record backing, validates tree depth <=6, checks root keys and vers fields, and performs an optional time-related record check. On success allocates a 0x34-byte sidr object owning the descriptor, copies identity24 and initializes dirty/cache fields. Destroys temporary backing on failure. Returns an internally mapped status; detailed policy constants remain encoded.

Requires a nonzero record offset with exactly four payload bytes. Reads its big-endian scalar through ReadRecordU32 and writes an affine-encoded output, rather than a plain integer. Returns the record/argument status; output is written only after successful length and read checks.

Shifts the encoded sign/magnitude integer in place: positive bits shift left, zero/negative bits shift right by the negated amount. Preserves sign and normalizes limb count; an excessive right shift produces zero. Caller supplies capacity. Tail-branches into shared shift implementations; callers ignore the incidental register result.

Finds a child using decoded parent/key arguments, then copies its leaf payload through CopyRecordPayloadEncoded with larger capacity allowed. Reads capacity from the encoded in/out word, which is replaced by encoded payload length on success. Returns argument, missing-child or copy status.
Null-safe cleanup of storage-record +0x64 (sidd). Releases the descriptor at +0, clears that pointer, overwrites the 0x28-byte object, and frees it. Returns zero.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Null context returns 0. Otherwise calls FairPlay_DestroyDecryptionContext and returns its 32-bit status; the obfuscation multipliers reduce to identity modulo 2^32. Used in failed context creation and through game cleanup wrapper 0804bb90. Does not release a storage-registry handle.

Validates the record and optionally publishes its two header keys at +4/+8 after byte decoding plus separate affine word encodings. Returns status. The output words are encoded and must not be compared directly with plain key constants.

Initializes caller-provided one and r_squared buffers to R mod modulus and R^2 mod modulus, and stores the negative inverse of the low modulus word. R is 2^(32 * modulus limb count). Assumes a valid odd nonzero modulus; does not allocate or validate buffer capacity.

Requires mutable unborrowed backing and a leaf record. Resizes the record if needed, then replaces its payload using (x*0xb5+0x24)*0xa7 byte conversion. Returns validation/resize status; caller keeps input valid across reallocation and supplies bytes of source.

Writes an encoded sign/count and encoded magnitude limbs for the signed input. Zero sets count to zero. Caller supplies output capacity; previously stored high limbs beyond the new count remain untouched.

Decodes key/parent argument words, finds the matching child and reads its four-byte payload through ReadRecordAffineScalar. Returns an error if required pointers/keys are invalid or the child/read fails. Output remains in the scalar helper's affine encoding.

Feeds ordinary input bytes, encoding them for the software 64-byte block path. SHA-1 with flag 0x100 can switch to a backend that stages 0x1000-byte chunks. Returns zero on success or backend error; null input returns bytes and zero length returns zero. May change backend ownership and state flags.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Searches registry at 089cb020 with record stride 0xb8 for an encoded handle match. Routes the selected record through FairPlay_RefreshStorageRecord with a transformed refresh_selector; returns the record pointer or null on lookup/refresh failure. This lookup can perform disk I/O through refresh. Selector encoding and complete handle-validation rules remain unresolved.

Sets context tag at +0, clears scratch pointer +4 and allocates AES scratch there. On scratch failure destroys the whole context through FairPlay_DestroyDecryptionContext. Returns mapped allocation status; callers must not reuse context after failure.

Rejects borrowed/read-only backing flags, inserts a child and converts input bytes into record encoding with x*0x8b. Copy direction follows source/destination order. Optionally writes new record offset and returns status. Caller must keep source valid across possible backing resize.
Returns one when selector is 0, 1 or 2, otherwise zero. The two internal multipliers cancel modulo 2^32, so the external selector is plain. Pure predicate; no memory writes.

Uses the record descriptor at object+0 to find root divi/keyB=1. Reads its first big-endian payload word; a missing divi writes zero. Requires object and output, returns status, and does not create the optional record.

Validates a scalar record, decodes payload bytes with multiplier 0x17 and copies in overlap-aware direction. Requires payload length <=capacity, or exact length when allow_larger_capacity=0. Optionally publishes an encoded copied-length word. Returns status; a zero capacity permits null output only for an empty payload.

Validates a leaf record and copies its payload using x*0x1b-0x14 byte encoding. Requires payload <= capacity, or exact equality when allow_larger_capacity=0. Optional encoded_bytes receives payload size * 0xbd7d7cff. Returns zero or descriptor/record/size error; supports either copy direction.

Exports magnitude as fixed-width big-endian bytes multiplied by 0xe9, with leading zero padding. Returns without writing if output_bytes is smaller than abs(decoded limb count)*4. Ignores sign and does not return a status.

Validates an encoded record and returns its offset, or zero on failure. Offset zero means root at 12. Decodes big-endian size (minimum 20), checks end bounds/overflow and, when child count at +14 is nonzero, walks exactly that many nested records and requires their lengths to fill the parent. Internal bytes decode by multiplication by 0x17.

Tests the decoded type against 50, 51, 60, 61, 70 and 80; returns plain 0/1. Used by verification-object construction/processing. Pure predicate; the higher-level meanings of these numeric types remain unresolved.

Walks ordinary big-endian child atoms starting at sinf+8, checking minimum size and end bounds. Captures frma as a native format word, sign/schi payload offsets and sizes, and three skcr words; marks schm presence. Success requires exact end and flags frma|schm|schi (0x0b). Caller initializes info; duplicate recognized atoms overwrite prior fields.

Initializes SHA-1 mode, digests two decoded 32-bit prefixes in first-prefix then second-prefix order, then the encoded input payload and finalizes to a 20-byte encoded digest. Checks input/output pointers. Returns zero on the completed path; intermediate digest statuses are not checked.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Checks an encoded context tag, releases nonnull scratch object at +4 through 082a7398, overwrites the 0x50-byte context through an obfuscated byte loop, then frees it with 08023ef0. Returns a 32-bit status; exact tag/error encoding is unresolved. Outer release wrapper handles null. Overwrite bytes are generated values rather than a simple zero-fill.

Rejects null descriptor or null backing pointer. If bit 1 of (flags_at_8 * 3) is clear, overwrites the decoded byte count from +4 and frees backing storage at +0. Then overwrites and frees the 12-byte descriptor. Returns zero on cleanup; ownership flags and length are encoded.

Allocates an owned record buffer and converts input bytes with ((byte*0x49)-1)*0xa7. includes_prefix selects a full-buffer copy versus adding a zero 12-byte prefix. Rejects null input and short prefixed data, propagates allocation errors, and publishes the descriptor on success. Caller supplies a valid output pointer.

Walks ASN.1 elements against 28-byte encoded rules, with a fixed 16-level traversal stack. Supports optional rules, child/next indices, expected-payload comparison and callbacks receiving a 20-byte OSOS_FairPlayASN1Match. Special tag -0x1000000 accepts several ASN.1 string tags. Returns parse/callback status; callbacks may mutate their context. Does not allocate.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Allocates a 0x24-byte sidv/sidl object, decodes its backing through 08303c98, then validates the record tree with maximum depth 3. Copies the 24-byte identity and decoded mode into the object on success. On failure destroys the descriptor, wipes/frees the object and returns status.

Validates parent and walks nested records in its payload, comparing decoded header key A/B. Returns matching child offset or zero; optional ordinal is one-based. Traversal relies on the parent validation and encoded record lengths.

Computes base^exponent mod modulus for encoded integers. Converts base into Montgomery form, scans exponent bits from most to least significant with square/conditional multiply, converts out and copies to output. Uses two fixed 524-byte stack workspaces; caller initializes mont and supplies valid sizes.

Initializes HMAC with an internally encoded key. Keys longer than 64 bytes are hashed first; prepares encoded inner/outer pads using XOR 0x36/0x5c, stores outer pad at +0x68 and feeds the 64-byte inner pad. Null or zero-length key returns without initializing state. sidr callers use a 24-byte encoded key and mode 2 (SHA-1).

Shifts encoded integer magnitude left in place by whole limbs and remaining bits, preserving sign, filling low limbs with zero and updating encoded count. Caller supplies enough capacity. Shared tail target of BigIntShift; argument order is bits then value.

Validates the user-ID argument and requires sidr version at +0x2c to equal 0x10000, then dispatches to ApplySidrRightsFromSidv with decoded/re-encoded scalar arguments. Returns mapped argument/version/processing status. Caller provides a valid sidr pointer.
Writes 0 to WDTCON (0x3c800000), then 0x0aa5 to SWRCON (0x3c500050) to request a software reset. Spins forever if reset has not yet occurred.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Calls locked hardware AES using input=scratch+4 pointer, output=scratch+8 pointer, supplied key/IV, selector 0 and a fixed length of 0x1000 bytes. Returns 0 on hardware status 0, otherwise 0xffff5b32. Caller 0831bf88 also places a byte count on the stack, but this wrapper never reads it; both scratch buffers must hold a full page.

Copies bytes sequentially to state+0 when both pointers are nonnull; returns zero after copying or 9 for a null pointer. Used by SHA feed for 0..63 trailing bytes. No local length/capacity check; caller must supply a nonnegative count fitting the partial block.
Returns the cached pointer to the imported 0x120-byte SysInfo at 0x08a1a330; initializes the pointer on first use.
Reads the boot-info record at offset 0x18. Requires SysI magic, then copies 0x120 bytes from its pointer into 0x08a1a330. Returns 0 on success or 0x52 for invalid magic.

Queries the prior resource-gate state for mask (0,1), enables that resource and clears control at MMIO 0x3c100000. Returns the previous gate-state token for RestoreHardware. Does not itself read a random word or acquire a mutex.
Polls MMIO 0x3c100000 until status bits 0..2 are nonzero, then returns the word at +4. Assumes hardware has been prepared. Has no timeout, error return or allocation.

Startup hardware gate: reads imported HwVr and requires Classic revision >= 0x0300. Failure writes the softupdt warm-boot tag then resets the SoC. Success writes diskmode and continues initialization. Entered via IRAM thunk 0x220036c8.
Formats %d, %u, %x/%X, %s and %c; emits SYS_WRITEC (3) and SYS_WRITE0 (4).

Walks the format string and ARM variadic argument words, emitting text through semihosting. Supports decimal, unsigned, hex, character, string and percent conversions with limited width handling. Literal spans are temporarily NUL-terminated by Semihost_WriteSpan, so format must be writable.

Null returns -50; an already-set byte 0 returns 0. Otherwise checks embedded path+4 using storage mode +0xc: an existing path returns 0xffff5b81; an absent path sets byte 0 and returns 0xffff5b80. This is a state/status query, not a simple exists boolean.

Checks buffered length <0x1000 and internal digest pointer, processes pending data without final padding, then exports the 64-byte partial block, counters and five byte-reversed chaining words. Clears workspace, releases backing and frees wrapper on success. Returns status; caller must clear its backend reference.
Decrements the shared control-block count. The last reference deletes the model through vtable +0x1c, releases its optional lock and frees the block. Clears the reference.
Initializes a shared model reference. A nonnull model gets a 12-byte control block with count 1; synchronized creates an additional lock. The last reference deletes the model through vtable +0x1c.
Releases the destination and copies the source control block with a retained count; self-assignment is unchanged. Returns destination.
Returns the model pointer from a shared-reference control block, or null for an empty reference.
Releases the reference-counted backing storage of the one-pointer C++ string. Leaves shared empty storage allocated.
Constructs the one-pointer C++ string from null-terminated text, copying nonempty text into owned storage. Returns the string object.
Finds or inserts a C++ string key in the resource-name map and returns its numeric ID slot.
Appends a copied 24-byte album row to a begin/end/capacity vector. Grows native storage when full and frees the previous allocation.
COLR 0x0dad00cd Background_Color: stock 0x00ffffff. Resource overrides alone do not affect built-in view background colors or MenuView_DrawRow's alternating gray.
COLR 0x0dad00ce System_Text_Color: stock 0x00000000, stored as little-endian RGB word. Consumers convert to RGBA bytes with opaque alpha.

COLR 0x0dad05d8, CoverFlow_Backside_Border_Color: RGB #7e8183. Referenced at View 0x0dad05e3 +0x68 by outer background element 0x0dad05e4, separate from top bitmap 0x0dad05da. This RGB is unique among native COLR entries. CFW maps its fill to #383838 when dark mode is on; alpha and the stock resource remain unchanged.

View 0x0dad05e3, CoverFlow backside template. Outer background uses COLR 0x0dad05d8 (#7e8183) at +0x68. The inset album-info background uses SORC 0x274 at +0x114, resolving top BMap 0x0dad05da. List background uses COLR 0x0dad05d9 (white) at +0x2b8. Border color is independent of the top bitmap.
Copies IRAM, DRAM code and initialized data to their runtime addresses using the relocation delta in r0. Clears IRAM BSS and branches to the relocated IRAM entry.
Zeroes IRAM BSS at 0x2200af98 (0x57dc bytes) and DRAM BSS at 0x08a18d64 (0x12244c bytes). The intermediate clear length is zero.
Transferred from 2.0.4; absolute addresses below refer to that version.

Runs at IRAM 220071b0. r0=output queue, r1=position. Stores position at +0x13c and all 32 slots +0x34..+0xb0. Common reset reached from queue rebuild 220072cc, metadata clear 22007294, and underrun recovery 22007260. Called around decoder repositioning in 220054a8 via those reset paths. Synthesized-audio history must be invalidated when these queue positions reset.
